svg.text: The Sleepy Dragons: the transfer (phase B)
On a noun an s means more; on a verb it means one. The First Page's habit picks the wrong form every time
one dragon snores, three sleep on; ink copies of the baby sneeze too
all four snore; the baby sneezes alone: the bubble, exactly
Children learn the plural s years before the verb's s (Brown's order of the 14
morphemes, §2.1). The dragons' six wishes link two or three choices each (two
clauses, or a pronoun and its verb) and have two subjects joined by "and".
The model (1,000 visits, the bar 5 of 6): the First Page's habit 0 %; copies the subject's
ending 0 %; the nearest noun 0 %; a coin 0.1 %; the idea 100 % (slips 4 %: 89.3 %).
